text:
rachel: hey all, quick bootstrap Q on my M2. followed the dotfiles but keep getting `Permission denied` for `npm i -g` and VSCode terminals sometimes show a different node than iTerm. any quick checklist?

 tom: welcome rachel! two quick things: 1) npm global perms -> use ~/.npm-global via ~/.npmrc (prefix) and add that bin to PATH. 2) VSCode vs iTerm mismatch usually PATH/init ordering: put asdf init and shims early in ~/.zprofile so GUI apps and terminals see it.

 rachel: can you paste the minimal lines you'd add to zprofile?

 lexi: minimal we use: `export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.asdf/bin:$PATH"` then `if command -v brew >/dev/null 2>&1; then export PATH="$(brew --prefix)/bin:$PATH"; fi` and finally `. "$(brew --prefix asdf)/libexec/asdf.sh"`. keep heavy stuff in .zshrc. open a new login shell after changing.

 rachel: i had asdf init in .zshrc. moved it to .zprofile and restarted terminal, still saw brew node first. ran `which -a node` and saw /opt/homebrew/bin/node before the asdf shim. how to make sure shims win?

 tom: ensure you export PATH with asdf shims before adding brew bin. example order matters. also run `asdf reshim` after installs and remove any old node installs you don't need (`brew uninstall node` if you won't use it). `which -a node` is your friend.

 rachel: npm permissions fixed with npmrc + PATH tweak. VSCode integrated terminal is still weird for extensions that spawn processes (prettier). any config there?

 lexi: set VSCode terminal to launch login shells: "terminal.integrated.shellArgs.osx": ["-l"] for zsh. for extensions, some run in the UI process and won't inherit shell PATH; we prefer installing formatters as project devDependencies so extension calls the workspace node. also `envFile` in launch.json helps for debug configs.

 rachel: small dotfiles question: dotfiles repo links vimrc and it clobbered my local tmux.conf. any safe sync pattern?

 tom: backup on link. our link script usually moves existing to `.pre-onboard` and then symlinks. open a PR if your script didn't. prefer stow for idempotence.

 setup-bot: Welcome @rachel! Quick links: dotfiles repo https://git.internal/redwood/dotfiles. Run onboarding: https://internal.redwood.dev/onboard. Join #dev-setup if you need a pairing session.

 rachel: thanks team, fixed both issues and documented my Mac quirks in the onboarding doc. appreciate the help :rocket:
